key_insight: Hardware-aware quantum circuit synthesis can be framed as a hybrid generative problem: discrete circuit layout plus continuous SU(2) gate parameters on the Lie group manifold.
engineering_relevance: This enables more realistic quantum compilation for near-term devices by matching both gate geometry and hardware connectivity constraints.
method: Circuit skeleton selector picks an entangling template compatible with hardware.
Lie-group diffusion generates single-qubit gates directly on SU(2) ≃ S3.
Supports constrained synthesis, including targets with intentionally large or small rotation angles.
evidence_signal: The approach is evaluated on three-qubit Hamiltonian simulation targets (Transverse Field Ising and Heisenberg-XXZ) and reported to outperform comparable baselines while exploring fidelity-complexity tradeoffs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the learned circuit selector and the availability of suitable hardware-specific templates, which could limit transfer across devices.
paper_title: Lie Group Diffusion Models for Hardware-Aware Quantum Circuit Synthesis
